items.name: Boksoondoga Makgeolli
items.description: A premium unfiltered makgeolli made with organic rice. Creamy texture with subtle sweetness and a remarkably clean finish. Often called the 'champagne of makgeolli.'

westernMatch.description: If you like unfiltered sake, you'll love this creamy rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Boksoondoga, please

items.name: Neurin Maul Makgeolli
items.description: A premium makgeolli from Baehaejung Doga (Slow Village Brewery), founded by master brewer Bae Hae-jung who revived forgotten slow-fermentation techniques. Unlike commercial makgeolli that ferments in days, Neurin Maul undergoes extended low-temperature fermentation for a silky, layered flavor with subtle lactic tang. The name means 'Slow Village,' reflecting a philosophy that great rice wine cannot be rushed.

westernMatch.description: If you like wheat beer, try this smooth rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Neurin Maul makgeolli, please

items.name: Jipyeong Makgeolli
items.description: A classic Korean makgeolli from a brewery established in 1925. Clean, light, and easy to drink. A great entry point for first-time makgeolli drinkers.

westernMatch.description: If you like easy-drinking lagers, start with this approachable rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Jipyeong makgeolli, please

items.name: Damgeumju Sparkling Makgeolli
items.description: A modern sparkling makgeolli with fine bubbles and bright acidity. Served chilled in a wine glass, it bridges traditional rice wine and contemporary cocktail culture.

westernMatch.description: If you like prosecco, try this sparkling Korean rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One glass of sparkling makgeolli, please

items.name: Geumjeongsanseong Makgeolli
items.description: A robust makgeolli from Busan made with 100% rice and hand-pressed nuruk (traditional fermentation starter). 500 years of tradition packed into every sip. Fuller body and higher ABV than typical makgeolli.

westernMatch.description: If you like full-bodied Belgian wheat beer, try this rich rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Geumjeongsanseong makgeolli, please

items.name: Seoul Jangsoo Makgeolli
items.description: The most iconic draft makgeolli in Seoul, found at every traditional Korean pub. Affordable, refreshing, and the go-to drink for a classic Korean drinking experience.

westernMatch.description: If you like ordering a draft pint at the pub, this is the Korean equivalent

orderPhrases.english: One kettle of Jangsoo makgeolli, please

items.name: Ihwaju (Pear Blossom Wine)
items.description: A restored Goryeo-dynasty recipe. Extremely thick and spoonable -- more like a rice pudding than a drink. Sweet-sour balance with rich grain aroma. A truly unique tasting experience.

westernMatch.description: If you like thick, sweet dessert wines, this spoonable rice wine is an adventure

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Ihwaju, please

items.name: Wolmae Makgeolli
items.description: Another Seoul classic, lighter and slightly sweeter than Jangsoo. Named after a character from the famous Korean folktale Chunhyangjeon. Easy drinking and widely available.

westernMatch.description: If you like light, easy-drinking ales like Kolsch, this is a great casual rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Wolmae makgeolli, please

items.name: Gyeongtakju Rose 12
items.description: A stunning pink makgeolli naturally colored with Korean red rice -- no artificial coloring. Higher ABV at 12% gives it wine-like depth. Beautiful to look at and even better to drink.

westernMatch.description: If you like rose wine, this pink rice wine is a must-try

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Gyeongtakju Rose, please

items.name: Golmok Makgeolli
items.description: A trendy craft makgeolli from a Seoul micro-brewery. Clean, crisp, and slightly carbonated. Popular among young Koreans and a bridge between craft beer and traditional makgeolli.

westernMatch.description: If you like dry craft cider, this crisp makgeolli hits the same spot

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Golmok makgeolli, please

items.name: Jirangjigyo Makgeolli
items.description: A premium makgeolli named after a Chinese proverb meaning 'friendship like orchid and iris.' Rich flavor with floral notes and higher alcohol content. Great for sharing among friends.

westernMatch.description: If you like complex Belgian ales, this high-ABV makgeolli has similar depth

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Jirangjigyo, please

items.name: Hwayo 41
items.description: A premium distilled soju from Kwangjuyo, the renowned Korean ceramics company that has been crafting fine pottery for over 40 years. Made from 100% Korean rice and distilled through a meticulous process that yields extraordinary purity -- clean, smooth, with a subtle grain sweetness at 41% ABV. Served in Kwangjuyo's own handcrafted ceramic cups, Hwayo bridges Korea's pottery heritage and its distilling tradition in one elegant experience.

westernMatch.description: If you like premium vodka, try this refined rice spirit

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Hwayo 41, please

items.name: Hwayo 25
items.description: The most approachable Hwayo, at 25% ABV. Smooth and mild with a clean rice sweetness. Perfect for those who want to explore premium soju without the high alcohol punch.

westernMatch.description: If you like smooth, sippable vodka, this lower-proof soju is an easy entry

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Hwayo 25, please

items.name: Andong Soju
items.description: Traditional distilled soju from Andong, handcrafted by master distiller Cho Ok-hwa using the sojutgori (traditional copper still) method passed down for centuries. Rich and complex at 45% ABV, with deep grain aromatics developed through a double-distillation process unique to the Andong region. Designated as Gyeongsangbuk-do Intangible Cultural Heritage, this spirit survived Japanese colonial prohibition and remains a symbol of Korean distilling resilience.

westernMatch.description: If you like complex whisky, try this heritage Korean spirit

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Andong soju, please

items.name: Ilpum Andong Soju Gold 40
items.description: A premium oak-aged Andong soju. Grain aroma blended with oak barrel aging creates a smooth, whisky-like finish. 40% ABV but drinks remarkably gentle.

westernMatch.description: If you like oak-aged bourbon, this barrel-blended Korean soju has similar warmth

orderPhrases.korean: 일품 안동소주 골드 한 병 주세요
orderPhrases.romanized: Ilpum Andong-soju goldeu han byeong juseyo
orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Ilpum Andong Soju Gold, please

items.name: Hallasan Soju
items.description: Jeju Island's local soju, made with water from Hallasan volcano's underground springs. Slightly softer and cleaner than mainland soju. A must-try while visiting Jeju.

westernMatch.description: If you drink vodka sodas, try this clean Korean spirit neat or with a mixer

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Hallasan, please

items.name: Chamisul Fresh
items.description: The world's best-selling spirit by volume. This is what most Koreans drink nightly at BBQ restaurants and bars. Not a craft spirit, but an essential Korean cultural experience.

westernMatch.description: If you drink well vodka, this is Korea's universal spirit -- order it to drink like a local

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Chamisul, please

items.name: Munbaeju
items.description: Designated as Important Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 86-1. Made from wheat, millet, and sorghum -- no fruit is used, yet it has a mysterious pear-like aroma (munbae = wild pear). Served at the 2000 Inter-Korean Summit.

westernMatch.description: If you like Italian grappa's aromatic complexity, Munbaeju's mysterious pear scent will fascinate you

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Munbaeju, please

items.name: Igangju
items.description: One of the Three Great Wines of Joseon Dynasty. Infused with pear, ginger, turmeric, and honey. Complex layers of sweetness, spice, and warmth. A true taste of Korean history.

westernMatch.description: If you like spiced rum's warmth and sweetness, Igangju's pear-ginger infusion is a revelation

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Igangju, please

items.name: Gamhongro
items.description: One of the Three Great Wines of Joseon, meaning 'sweet red dew.' Triple-distilled and infused with herbs, creating a reddish hue and complex sweet-bitter finish. Made by Food Master artisan Lee Ki-sook.

westernMatch.description: If you like Italian amaro's herbal complexity, Gamhongro offers a similar bitter-sweet journey

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Gamhongro, please

items.name: Gosorisul
items.description: Jeju's traditional distilled spirit, Intangible Cultural Heritage of Jeju. Made from millet with a sweet grain aroma and surprisingly gentle feel despite 40% ABV. 'Gosori' refers to the traditional Jeju still.

westernMatch.description: If you like mezcal's earthy, artisanal character, Gosorisul has similar craft spirit depth

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Gosorisul, please

items.name: Gyeongju Beopju
items.description: Korea's most celebrated cheongju (clear rice wine), brewed by the Choi family of Gyeongju for over 300 years across multiple generations. Designated as Important Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 86-3, it uses a secret nuruk recipe passed down through the family. Refined and elegant with a golden hue, it was traditionally served at ancestral rites and royal banquets -- a living thread connecting modern Korea to the Silla Dynasty.

westernMatch.description: If you like premium sake, you'll appreciate this refined Korean rice wine

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Gyeongju Beopju, please

items.name: Kooksoondang Cheongju
items.description: A widely available premium cheongju. Crystal clear with a delicate rice aroma and clean finish. Good for those exploring Korean clear rice wine for the first time.

westernMatch.description: If you like everyday-quality sake, this is a great Korean equivalent

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Kooksoondang cheongju, please

items.name: Hansan Sogokju
items.description: Called 'the wine that makes you sit down' because it's so delicious you can't stop drinking. Sweet, umami-rich yakju (medicinal wine) from Chungnam province, with 1,500 years of history. Exported to the US and Japan.

westernMatch.description: If you like sweet sherry's depth, Sogokju's rich umami sweetness is equally addictive

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Hansan Sogokju, please

items.name: Baekseju
items.description: Meaning '100-year wine,' this herbal rice wine is infused with 12 herbs and ginseng. Nutty, slightly medicinal flavor. A staple at Korean BBQ restaurants, often ordered as a lighter alternative to soju.

westernMatch.description: If you like herbal vermouth, Baekseju's ginseng-infused flavor is a Korean parallel

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Baekseju, please

items.name: Chuseongju
items.description: An herbal rice wine from Damyang, infused with omija (five-flavor berry) and eucommia bark. Comes in a distinctive bamboo-shaped bottle. Complex medicinal-sweet flavor with beautiful amber color.

westernMatch.description: If you like herbal digestifs, Chuseongju's medicinal complexity is worth exploring

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Chuseongju, please

items.name: Sansachun
items.description: A red-tinted rice wine made with Chinese hawthorn berries. Sweet, tart, and fruity with a refreshing finish. Considered a 'medicinal alcohol' for over 400 years. Easy to find at most Korean restaurants.

westernMatch.description: If you like fruity sangria, Sansachun's sweet-tart berry flavor is an easy match

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Sansachun, please

items.name: Maehwasu Plum Wine
items.description: A Korean plum wine made with maehwa (apricot blossom) extract, distinct from Japanese umeshu which uses ume plum. Delicate floral sweetness with a lighter, more perfumed character -- less syrupy than its Japanese cousin. Best enjoyed during Korea's spring maehwa festivals in Gwangyang and Yangsan, where blossoms and plum wine are a centuries-old pairing.

westernMatch.description: If you like umeshu (plum wine), try this Korean version

orderPhrases.english: One glass of plum wine, please

items.name: Bokbunjaju (Black Raspberry Wine)
items.description: A deep ruby wine made from Korean black raspberries (bokbunja). Rich berry aroma, sweet-tart balance, and believed to have health-boosting properties. Available at every convenience store.

westernMatch.description: If you like ruby port's berry richness, Bokbunjaju has similar depth at lower ABV

orderPhrases.english: One glass of black raspberry wine, please

items.name: Maesilju (Green Plum Wine)
items.description: Made from Korean green plums (maesil), this is one of Korea's most beloved fruit wines. Sweet-sour with a bright, refreshing finish. Different from Japanese umeshu -- lighter and more tart.

westernMatch.description: If you like limoncello's sweet-tart citrus kick, maesilju's plum tanginess is a perfect match

orderPhrases.english: One glass of green plum wine, please

items.name: Myungjak Omijaju
items.description: Made from omija (Schisandra, the 'five-flavor berry') -- sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and pungent all in one sip. A naturally fermented wine with beautiful pink color and complex taste experience.

westernMatch.description: If you like aromatic white wines, omijaju's complex flavor profile will intrigue you

orderPhrases.english: One glass of omija wine, please

items.name: Jeju Gamgyulju (Citrus Wine)
items.description: A bright, aromatic wine made from Jeju Island's famous tangerines. Citrusy, fresh, and slightly sweet. Perfect souvenir from Jeju and a refreshing summer drink.

westernMatch.description: If you like Aperol spritz's citrusy sweetness, Jeju tangerine wine is a natural alternative

orderPhrases.english: One glass of tangerine wine, please

items.name: Gohung Yujaju (Yuzu Wine)
items.description: Made from Korean yuzu (yuja) grown in Goheung, Jeollanam-do. Intensely aromatic with bright citrus notes. Low ABV makes it dangerously drinkable. Popular as a trendy new traditional drink.

westernMatch.description: If you love yuzu in cocktails, try it in Korean wine form -- pure and unadulterated

orderPhrases.english: One glass of yuzu wine, please

items.name: Seokryu Yiyagi (Pomegranate Wine)
items.description: A exotic pomegranate wine with deep garnet color. Tart, tannic, and slightly sweet with a wine-like body. A great alternative for grape wine lovers looking to try something Korean.

westernMatch.description: If you like light-bodied red wines, this pomegranate wine has a similar elegance

orderPhrases.english: One glass of pomegranate wine, please

items.name: Meoruju (Wild Grape Wine)
items.description: Made from Korean wild grapes (meoru) that grow on mountain vines. More intense and tannic than cultivated grapes. Full-bodied with earthy, berry flavors. Korea's answer to natural wine.

westernMatch.description: If you love natural wines, meoruju's wild grape character is an authentic Korean terroir expression

orderPhrases.english: One glass of wild grape wine, please

items.name: Ma She Blanc
items.description: A refreshing sparkling citrus wine from Jeju, blending traditional makgeolli technique with tangerine. Low ABV, fizzy, and perfect for a summer day. The name is a pun on 'drink' (ma-sheo) and 'blanc.'

westernMatch.description: If you like citrus hard seltzers, this Korean sparkling citrus wine is a natural upgrade

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Ma She Blanc, please

items.name: Gukhwaju (Chrysanthemum Wine)
items.description: A fragrant flower wine infused with chrysanthemum petals. Traditionally brewed in autumn during the chrysanthemum festival. Floral, delicate, and slightly herbal. A seasonal specialty.

westernMatch.description: If you like elderflower liqueur's delicate floral character, chrysanthemum wine is its Korean counterpart

orderPhrases.english: One glass of chrysanthemum wine, please

items.name: Dugyeonju (Azalea Wine)
items.description: A rare spring wine made with azalea petals, giving it a delicate pink hue. One of Korea's most romantic traditional wines. Sweet, floral, and only available in limited quantities.

westernMatch.description: If you love floral liqueurs, this azalea-petal wine is a rare Korean treasure

orderPhrases.english: One glass of azalea wine, please

items.name: Dansul (Sweet Rice Drink)
items.description: Barely alcoholic sweet rice drink -- basically the earliest stage of the makgeolli fermentation process. Sweet, grainy, and comforting. Great for non-drinkers who want to experience Korean brewing culture.

westernMatch.description: If you know Japanese amazake, dansul is its Korean cousin -- sweet, grainy, barely alcoholic

orderPhrases.english: One glass of sweet rice drink, please

items.name: Chamisul Peach Soju
items.description: Fruit-flavored soju that started the K-soju craze worldwide. Sweet peach flavor makes this an easy entry for anyone new to Korean drinking culture. Extremely popular with international tourists.

westernMatch.description: If you like peach schnapps or sweet cocktails, fruit soju is an instant favorite

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of peach soju, please

items.name: Chamisul Green Grape Soju
items.description: Green grape flavored soju -- one of the most popular flavored soju varieties. Sweet and refreshing with a candy-like grape taste. The viral 'Korean soju' flavor that took TikTok by storm.

westernMatch.description: If you like sweet grape alcopops, this K-soju started a global craze

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of green grape soju, please

items.name: Good Day Soju
items.description: Busan's local soju, a must-try when visiting the port city. Made with natural alkaline water. Slightly sweeter and smoother than Seoul's Chamisul. Ask any Busan local -- they'll tell you it's better.

westernMatch.description: Like trying the local vodka brand in any country -- a Busan drinking essential

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Good Day, please

items.name: Cheoeum Cheoreom
items.description: Chamisul's main rival, made with alkaline water from Gangwon-do. The name means 'like the first time.' Slightly softer on the palate. Try both and pick your side -- it's a national debate.

westernMatch.description: If Chamisul is Smirnoff, Cheoeum Cheoreom is Absolut -- the eternal rivalry

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Cheoeum Cheoreom, please

items.name: Somaek (Soju + Beer Bomb)
items.description: Not a product but a cultural ritual: drop a shot of soju into a glass of beer. The golden ratio is 3:7 (soju:beer). Every Korean knows how to make it. Learn the technique and you'll make instant friends.

westernMatch.description: Like a boilermaker -- drop a shot of soju into beer and chug. Korea's favorite drinking ritual

orderPhrases.english: Can you make a somaek for me, please?

items.name: Nuruk Makgeolli (House Makgeolli)
items.description: House-made makgeolli found at traditional makgeolli bars. Each place has its own recipe. Ask 'jip makgeolli isseoyo?' (Do you have house makgeolli?). The real authentic experience.

westernMatch.description: Like asking for the house wine in Italy -- every place has their own character

orderPhrases.english: Do you have house makgeolli?

items.name: Hwayo X Premium
items.description: The lightest in the Hwayo lineup at 17% ABV. Designed for easy sipping, smooth enough to drink neat or on the rocks. A gateway to premium Korean soju for craft cocktail enthusiasts.

westernMatch.description: If you like sipping light spirits on the rocks, Hwayo X is a refined choice

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Hwayo X, please

items.name: Hwayo 53
items.description: The pinnacle of Hwayo's range at 53% ABV. Crystal clear and intensely pure. Despite the high proof, it goes down with surprising grace. For serious spirit enthusiasts only.

westernMatch.description: If you appreciate cask strength whisky, Hwayo 53 is a purist's Korean spirit

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Hwayo 53, please

items.name: Hansan Sogokju Clear
items.description: The filtered clear version of Hansan Sogokju. More refined and lighter than the original, with the same addictive sweet-umami character. Like the difference between unfiltered and filtered sake.

westernMatch.description: If you like refined filtered sake, this clear version of Sogokju is delicate and compelling

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Hansan Sogokju Clear, please

items.name: Korean Grape Wine (Podoju)
items.description: Korea has its own wine region in Yeongdong, Chungcheong-do. Made with Korean grapes (Campbell Early), these wines are lighter and fruitier than European wines. A surprisingly pleasant discovery.

westernMatch.description: If you like light, fruity Beaujolais, Korean grape wine has a similar easy-drinking character

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Korean wine, please

items.name: Jinro 24 Gold
items.description: A premium version of Korea's most iconic soju brand. Higher ABV than standard Chamisul, with bamboo charcoal filtering for extra smoothness. The gold label signals 'stepping up' from regular soju.
items.oneLiner: A step up from basic soju

westernMatch.description: If you drink mid-range vodka, Jinro Gold is the Korean equivalent -- better than basic

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Jinro Gold, please

items.name: Gamnoju (Persimmon Wine)
items.description: A golden wine made from dried persimmons (gotgam), a Korean autumn specialty. Honey-like sweetness with warm spice notes. Pairs beautifully with Korean desserts.

westernMatch.description: If you like honeyed, late harvest wines, persimmon wine's autumn sweetness is a match

orderPhrases.english: One glass of persimmon wine, please

items.name: Banana Makgeolli
items.description: A fun, banana-flavored makgeolli that tastes like a banana milkshake with a slight kick. Not traditional, but wildly popular with tourists and at convenience stores. Great for makgeolli beginners.

westernMatch.description: If you like banana cocktails, this bottled banana rice wine is pure fun

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of banana makgeolli, please

items.name: Dongdongju
items.description: Similar to makgeolli but with floating rice grains on top (dong-dong = floating). A rustic, traditional drinking experience. Served in a large brass pot (jugeonja) and scooped with a ladle.

westernMatch.description: Like a farmhouse cider with bits of apple -- rustic, honest, and charming

orderPhrases.english: One pot of dongdongju, please

items.name: Omegisul
items.description: Jeju's unique millet wine, exclusive to the island. Made with Jeju's native millet (omegi) and nuruk. Sweet and slightly tart with a distinctive grain character. The base for Jeju's traditional Gosorisul distillation.

westernMatch.description: If you like funky farmhouse ales, Omegisul's millet character has similar artisanal depth

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Omegisul, please

items.name: Idong Makgeolli
items.description: A rustic, full-flavored makgeolli from Pocheon, famous for its strong nuruk (fermentation starter) character. Thicker and earthier than most — this is the countryside grandmother's recipe. A favorite among Koreans who prefer bold, traditional flavors over modern smooth styles.

westernMatch.description: If you like rough, unfiltered farmhouse cider, this raw makgeolli has the same honest character

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Idong makgeolli, please

items.name: Kooksoondang Raw Makgeolli
items.description: A widely available unfiltered makgeolli with more depth than typical convenience store options. Made with 100% rice and traditional nuruk, it has a grainy, slightly tangy richness. The best bang-for-your-buck complex makgeolli — find it at any Korean convenience store.

westernMatch.description: If you like cloudy, unfiltered German Kellerbier, this raw makgeolli has similar grainy depth

orderPhrases.english: One bottle of Kooksoondang raw makgeolli, please

items.name: Bongpyeong Buckwheat Makgeolli
items.description: A small-batch makgeolli from Bongpyeong, Pyeongchang — the literary village immortalized by Lee Hyo-seok's novel 'When Buckwheat Flowers Bloom.' Made with local buckwheat instead of pure rice for a nuttier, earthier finish than typical makgeolli.
items.oneLiner: Buckwheat from a literary highland village

westernMatch.description: If you like cloudy, grain-forward wheat beer, this nutty buckwheat makgeolli will feel familiar

orderPhrases.english: Do you have Bongpyeong buckwheat makgeolli?

items.name: Jeongseon Deodeokju
items.description: An infusion-style yakju from the steep mountains of Jeongseon, made with wild deodeok root (Codonopsis lanceolata) — a prized Korean medicinal plant. Earthy, slightly bitter, with a clean herbal finish. Long served as a tonic for stamina in Gangwon's mountain villages.
items.oneLiner: Mountain root tonic from Gangwon's deep valleys

westernMatch.description: If you like bittersweet herbal Italian Amaro, this rooty Korean tonic plays in the same register

orderPhrases.situation: Asking at a herbal liquor shop
orderPhrases.english: One glass of Jeongseon deodeok liquor, please

items.name: Yangyang Songiju
items.description: A rare yakju from Yangyang, Gangwon — Korea's most famous pine mushroom (songi) region. Whole pine mushrooms are infused into rice wine, lending an unmistakable forest-floor aroma. Traditionally drunk during the brief autumn songi harvest.
items.oneLiner: Korea's prized pine mushroom in a glass

westernMatch.description: If you like earthy, mushroomy whites with rich umami, this Korean equivalent will surprise you

orderPhrases.english: Do you have Yangyang pine mushroom liquor?

items.name: Jindo Hongju
items.description: Korea's only red liquor. Distilled rice spirit is filtered through jicho (purple gromwell root), which dyes it a brilliant ruby color and adds a faint herbal note. A regional specialty of Jindo island in South Jeolla, designated a Korean intangible cultural property.
items.oneLiner: Korea's one and only red distilled spirit

westernMatch.description: If you like clear infused spirits like Scandinavian aquavit, Jindo Hongju brings a dramatic Korean color and subtle herbal twist

items.tags: red, herbal, premium, ceremonial, jeolla, intangible-heritage

orderPhrases.english: One glass of Jindo Hongju, please

items.name: Songhwa Baekiljoo
items.description: A legendary temple-tradition spirit from Sukwangsa monastery on Mt. Moaksan, Wanju. Pine pollen (songhwa) is fermented with rice and aged a full 100 days before being distilled. Designated a Korean intangible cultural property and one of Korea's most prestigious traditional liquors.

westernMatch.description: If you like complex distilled spirits with floral and herbal layers, this monastery-aged Korean spirit deserves the same reverence

items.tags: temple, premium, distilled, pine, intangible-heritage, ceremonial

orderPhrases.situation: At a premium Korean restaurant or duty-free
orderPhrases.english: May I have a glass of Songhwa Baekiljoo, please?

items.name: Jukryeokgo
items.description: A medicinal liquor from Jeongeup, Jeollabuk-do — distilled with bamboo extract (jukryeok) along with pine and ginger. Recorded in Joseon-era medical texts and once prescribed as a remedy for fever and heat. Today it's a cult traditional spirit, one of the 'Three Great Liquors of the South.'

westernMatch.description: If you like complex herbal liqueurs like Chartreuse, this Korean medicinal cousin earns its place on the same shelf

items.tags: medicinal, herbal, bamboo, premium, intangible-heritage, three-great-liquors

orderPhrases.situation: At a traditional Korean liquor specialty shop
orderPhrases.korean: 죽력고 한 잔 주실 수 있나요?
orderPhrases.romanized: Jukryeokgo han jan jusil su innayo?
orderPhrases.english: Could I have a glass of Jukryeokgo?
